newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ruling coalition says stands by Deve Gowda.
newsitem.headline: India's ruling coalition says stands by Deve Gowda.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition said on Thursday that it would not agree to the Congress party's demand that Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda step down.

United Front leader Harkishen Singh Surjeet told a news conference that the 15-party centre-left ruling alliance was prepared to face a vote of confidence in parliament set for Friday, but was still willing to hold talks with Congress.

"Our stand is final. There is no question of a change of leadership," Surjeet told reporters after the United Front's decision-making Steering Committee held a meeting to take stock of the political crisis.
Earlier on Thursday, Congress said it would vote against Deve Gowda in the confidence motion if the United Front refused to change it leader.
"It is for the people to judge, the parliament to judge," Surjeet said. "Whatever happens, we will face parliament.

But Surjeet, who is the general secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), held open the door to possible further talks with Congress. "Till tomorrow morning, if something happens, then we will see," he said.
